_steps.what: Any system component creates a bridge item: user_request (User via API), task_completed/task_failed (Scheduler), worker_message (Worker mid-task), health_alert (HealthMonitor), governance_decision (Governance).
bridge.enqueue(managerId, { type, source, payload, priority }). Item enters per-project FIFO queue with priority tier.
If Manager is idle: spawn immediately with this item. If Manager is busy: item waits in queue (FIFO within priority tier).

Manager receives ONE item as event prompt. Follows todo list. For user_request: assess, design workflow, create task, approve, report. For task_completed: read output, review, apply, build, commit, docs, report. For worker_message: read, respond (provide files or relay to user).
Manager process exits. bridge.setManagerIdle(managerId). If queue has more items: spawn again. If empty: do nothing. Zero cost.

_tags: @gotcha("Git commands timeout after 10 seconds. If git is unavailable, return empty results.")
_steps.what: Git commit lands, or periodic check runs, or manager requests drift detection. GenomeAgent.getRecentCommits() fetches recent git log entries. For each commit: analyzeCommit(hash) extracts changed files via git diff-tree.
mapFilesToComponents(files) matches changed files against component entry fields in genome.yaml frontmatter. Returns ComponentMatch[] with direct matches.
For each matched component, parse frontmatter to get depends_on list. Mark both matched component and its dependencies as potentially affected.

detectDrift() scans ALL components for: missing source files (entry points to deleted file), missing genome .md files (genome.yaml lists file that does not exist), broken dependency references (depends_on points to non-existent component). Returns DriftIssue[] with severity (error/warning).
detectNewFiles() scans packages/node/src/ for .ts files not tracked in any component entry field. These are candidates for new genome component entries.

_tags: @gotcha("Scoped context generation failures are non-critical. Workspace creation proceeds without Layer 8 if it fails.")
_steps.what: Drift issues injected into manager event prompt via buildPromptFromBridgeItem() for task_completed events. Manager decides: update genome (code is right) or fix code (genome is right).

When a task workspace is built, GenomeAgent provides scoped context via getScopedContext(). Injected as Layer 8 in worker CLAUDE.md. Algorithm: match affected files to components, resolve depends_on (1 level deep), keyword-match task description, find related flows and rules. Cap at maxComponents (default 8).

nodes.summary: How the Project Genome stays in sync with code reality. GenomeAgent analyzes commits, maps files to components, detects drift, and provides scoped context to workers. Zero cost (all local operations).

_tags: @gotcha("Requires 10 Lux stake to propose. New identities with < 10 Lux cannot propose upgrades.")
_steps.what: Any node creates a proposal via POST /governance/propose {title, description, type}. Types: general, code_upgrade, parameter_change, budget. Proposal synced to all nodes via GossipSub.
Nodes comment on proposals during configurable discussion period. Comments synced via P2P.

Each node casts one vote: approve or reject via POST /governance/vote {proposalId, vote}. Votes weighted by reputation. Min reputation gate: low-rep nodes cannot vote on critical proposals. Votes synced via GossipSub.
Quorum reached OR time expires triggers decision. Standard: 51% majority with 30% quorum. Emergency: 40% quorum, 1-hour vote period. Decision: approved or rejected.
If approved: code_upgrade triggers upgrade-protocol flow, parameter_change applied by manager, general creates task from proposal, budget adjusts budget settings.
Proposer gets 5.0 Lux if approved. Voters get 0.1 Lux each via emission witness. Lux minted for governance participation.

_steps.what: PandoNode.start() calls AgentManager.start(). AgentManager creates pando-node-mgr Agent (role=manager). Starts Bridge Watcher (event-driven, no timer).

Agent.buildClaudeMd() generates 4-layer CLAUDE.md template: Layer 1 (role principles from genome/templates/manager.md), Layer 2 (project context from project-state.md and scoped genome components), Layer 3 (learned lessons auto-updated from experience), Layer 4 (current task). Writes to ~/.pando/agents/{id}/workspace/.
Agent ready to receive events. No process spawned yet. Zero cost while idle.

Any source enqueues item to bridge: user_request (User via API), task_completed/task_failed (Scheduler), worker_message (Worker mid-task), health_alert (HealthMonitor), governance_decision (Governance).

_tags: @gotcha("Per-event spawn: claude -p --continue --resume <sessionId>. stdin=ignore. Delete CLAUDECODE env var from child process.")
_steps.what: If Manager is idle: item = bridge.next(managerId), spawn claude -p with prompt, --output-format stream-json --verbose --dangerously-skip-permissions --model claude-sonnet-4-6. If sessionId exists: --continue --resume <sessionId>. If Manager is busy: item waits in queue (FIFO within priority tier).

Manager receives single-item event prompt. Follows todo list workflow (dynamic per item type). For code tasks: includes commit + genome DOCS step. Process runs, responds, exits. Session ID captured from first spawn for continuity.
Bridge watcher detects Manager process exit. Sets manager status to idle. If bridge queue has more items, spawn again with next item. If empty, do nothing. Zero cost when idle.

_tags: @gotcha("Bridge queue persisted to disk. Items survive restarts and crashes.")
_steps.what: If Claude CLI not found: status=failed, items stay in queue. If spawn times out (5 min): process killed, item re-queued (max 3 retries). If spawn exits non-zero: warning logged, in-flight item re-queued. Session ID cleared on hard failure.

On node shutdown: AgentManager.stopAll() sends SIGTERM to all child processes, waits 10s, SIGKILL remaining. AgentManager.stop() stops bridge watcher, persists agent state. Bridge queue preserved for restart.

nodes.summary: How a manager session starts, runs, and recovers from crashes. Driven by the Bridge Queue with zero-cost idle. No timers, no polling.

_steps.what: Clone repo, npm install, npm run build. Or use launcher: start-node.command (Mac) / start-node.bat (Windows).
node packages/node/dist/cli.js --port 4001. Or double-click launcher. Node process starts running.

_tags: @gotcha("On subsequent runs, auto-loads existing identity. Only prompts for password if identity is encrypted.")
_steps.what: TUI silently auto-creates identity on first run (no prompts). Ed25519 keypair generated, encrypted with password (PBKDF2 + AES-256-GCM). Stored in ~/.pando/identities/{peerId}.json. Session cached in ~/.pando/session.json.

_tags: @gotcha("Without operator login, node earns no Lux rewards. It operates as relay-only.")
_steps.what: TUI checks for ~/.pando/operator-session.json (auto-login). If found and valid: restores operator state. If not found: node runs as relay-only (no rewards). Operator can /login or /register at any time. On login, node registers itself under user account via POST /auth/me/nodes.
If --bootstrap provided: connect to known peer. If no bootstrap: mDNS discovers local peers. Known-peers from previous sessions are dialed automatically. Auto-connects to EC2 bootstrap by default.

_tags: @gotcha("Nodes behind NAT (home Windows/Mac) connect outbound to cloud nodes. Cloud nodes cannot dial back to NAT nodes. This is expected.")
_steps.what: 5s after first peer connects: receives PEER_EXCHANGE with addresses of other nodes in the network. Dials them to form a full mesh. Re-exchange at 30s and 90s catches late-connecting peers. See flow PeerExchange.
LedgerSync requests missing transactions from peers. GossipSub subscribes to all topics. Transactions applied in order until consistent with network state.
First-time node registration: receives genesis Lux. Early multiplier: accounts 1-100 get 5x, 101-1000 get 3x, 1001-10000 get 2x.
API server listening on --api-port (default 4000). P2P listening on --port. Optional: start gateway, scheduler (--scheduler), monitor (--monitor). Full node operational.

nodes.summary: How a new node joins the Pando network. Install, start, create identity, optionally login as operator, connect to peers, sync ledger, receive genesis allocation, and become fully operational.

_tags: @gotcha("Eight GossipSub topics: pando/transactions, pando/tasks, pando/governance, pando/resources, pando/reputation, pando/content, pando/capabilities, pando/prices.")
_steps.what: Node creates a state change (transaction, capability update, governance vote, content record). Publishes to the appropriate GossipSub topic.
All connected nodes receive the message via GossipSub. Each node validates: signature, balance (for transactions), dedup check.
Valid state change applied to local store. Account balances updated for transactions. Content records merged by version. Capabilities refreshed with 15-min TTL.

On reconnect, nodes request missing state since last sync (catch-up). Conflict resolution: transactions dedup by hash, task claiming is First-Claim-Wins with timestamp tiebreak, governance votes are additive, capabilities are latest-wins per node, content uses version-number-wins.

nodes.summary: How state replicates across all nodes in the network via GossipSub topics. Covers transaction sync, governance, capabilities, content, and conflict resolution strategies.

_steps.what: Node A creates transaction (transfer or emission). LedgerSync publishes to pando/transactions topic.
All connected nodes receive via GossipSub. Each validates: Ed25519 signature, sufficient balance, dedup by tx hash.
Valid transaction applied to local ledger. Account balances updated. Duplicate transactions silently skipped.
Catch-up on reconnect: nodes request missing transactions since last sync point.

_steps.what: AI or human commits a fix, pushes to GitHub. Calls POST /upgrade/propose { description }. Creates governance proposal with current commit hash.
Dev mode (8 or fewer active peers): governance auto-approves instantly. Live mode (>8 peers): nodes vote, supermajority (>66%) required.

_tags: @gotcha("Build timeout: 180s. If build fails, automatic rollback to previous commit.")
_steps.what: Proposing node runs git pull, verifies commit hash matches governance-approved hash, npm run build, restart.
After successful local upgrade, broadcasts upgrade_available notification via GossipSub pando/upgrades topic. Includes commitHash, description.
Each peer receives notification, runs git pull, verifies commit hash, builds, restarts. Restart exit code 75 signals PM2/launcher to restart.

_tags: @gotcha("No single point of failure. Even if proposer dies after governance approval, all peers eventually catch up.")
_steps.what: Catch-up timer runs every 5 minutes (30s startup delay). Scans governance for passed upgrade proposals not yet applied. If proposer went offline before broadcasting, peers still discover and apply the upgrade independently.
All nodes running new code. Version-pinned nodes refuse upgrade. Emergency rollback available via POST /upgrade/rollback (fast-track governance vote).

nodes.summary: P2P self-upgrade protocol (Phase 82). AI or human commits fix, pushes to GitHub, proposes upgrade via governance, all nodes pull + verify + build + restart. Catch-up timer ensures no node misses an upgrade.

_tags: @gotcha("identify protocol takes 1-3s to complete. updateKnownPeer is delayed 3s to ensure peerStore has announce addresses before persisting.")
_steps.what: New peer connects via bootstrap or known-peers dial. libp2p identify protocol runs automatically, exchanging listen/announce addresses. Announce addresses (public IPs) are stored in the peerStore.

_tags: @gotcha("EC2 nodes in the same VPC connect via internal IPs (172.31.x.x). Without peerStore addresses, known-peers would only store internal IPs that external nodes cannot dial.")
_steps.what: updateKnownPeer() saves both connection addresses AND peerStore announce addresses to ~/.pando/known-peers.json. This ensures public IPs are persisted even when the actual TCP connection uses internal/VPC IPs.

5s after connect: node sends PEER_EXCHANGE message to the new peer. Payload contains all connected peers' addresses (connection addrs + known-peers + peerStore announce addrs). Filtered to exclude the recipient's own address.

_tags: @gotcha("Nodes behind NAT (home Windows/Mac) cannot be dialed from cloud nodes. They connect outbound. This is expected — peer exchange helps them discover cloud nodes, not the other way around.")
_steps.what: Receiving node parses peer list, skips already-connected peers, tries to dial each unknown peer using the shared addresses. Tries all addresses for each peer until one works.
Delayed re-exchange at 30s and 90s after boot broadcasts the full peer list to all connected peers. This catches peers that connected after the initial 5s exchange window.

Combined with known-peers persistence (7-day TTL, 50-peer cap), peer exchange ensures full mesh formation within ~90s of boot. On restart, known-peers are dialed immediately, providing instant reconnection.

nodes.summary: Peer exchange protocol — nodes share peer addresses on connect so new nodes can form a full mesh without a central hub. Replaces the need for a relay/bootstrap hub.

_steps.what: Every 5 minutes, select a random connected peer.

_tags: @gotcha("With fewer than 6 peers, GossipSub mesh may be too thin for reliable message propagation. This timer ensures governance decisions reach all nodes regardless.")
_steps.what: Request governance catch-up from the selected peer. Peer sends all proposals/votes/decisions the requesting node hasn't seen.
Apply received governance state. This catches upgrade proposals, votes, and decisions that were missed via GossipSub.

nodes.summary: Periodic governance re-sync — every 5 minutes, nodes request governance state from a random peer. Safety net for thin GossipSub meshes where votes/decisions may not propagate.

_tags: @gotcha("P2PStorageBackend means ThreadStore, ProjectStore, etc. always initialize. No more 'if (!threadStore) return 503'.")
_steps.what: Create P2PStorageBackend implementing StorageBackend interface (6 methods). Finds compute peers via CapabilityRegistry (storageBackend=mongodb). Forwards operations via P2P request-reply (pando/storage-proxy). Failover: tries next compute peer on timeout.
In node startup: if PANDO_STORAGE_URL set, use MongoStorageBackend. If not set, use P2PStorageBackend (instead of leaving null). Every node gets a StorageBackend.
Remove CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY and PANDO_STORAGE_URL from untrusted nodes (Lightsail, Windows). Restart. Node auto-uses P2PStorageBackend.
Test ALL features from untrusted node: search, governance, chat threads, projects. Verify zero 503 errors.

_tags: @gotcha("Agent work happens on untrusted nodes. Data lives on EC2. Real-time via BridgeQueue AND persistent via P2PStorageBackend.")
_steps.what: Full agent workflow E2E from untrusted node with Claude Code: chat message triggers project, manager agent spawns locally, builds something, messages persist to MongoDB via P2P, close/reopen browser confirms history intact.
POST /projects/:id/deploy tries all running EC2 instances, not just first. On timeout/failure, tries next instance.

_tags: @gotcha("Only thing that dies with a node is the agent workspace (ephemeral). Everything else is in MongoDB, GitHub, S3, or P2P-synced.")
_steps.what: Kill one EC2. Verify P2PStorageBackend routes to survivor. Chat and project reads still work. Redeploy goes to surviving EC2. Bring original back, network self-heals.

nodes.summary: Phase 83: Network hardening and compute failover. Transform from dev mode (all nodes have everything) to two-tier trust (untrusted nodes use P2PStorageBackend, compute nodes have MongoDB). Every user-facing feature must work from an untrusted node.

_steps.what: Chat messages and project records: MongoDB via P2PStorageBackend. Survives node crash and EC2 death (MongoDB is external). Agent workspace: local filesystem (ephemeral). Does NOT survive node crash.

_tags: @gotcha("The workspace is reconstructable from GitHub. That is the key design principle.")
_steps.what: Project code: GitHub (survives everything). Deployed apps: S3 Tier 1 survives EC2 death, Tier 2 needs redeploy. Ledger/governance: P2P-synced (survives everything). Credentials: MongoDB + master key on EC2 only (survives EC2 death via external MongoDB).

nodes.summary: Data persistence layers in the hardened network. What survives node crashes and EC2 failures.

_tags: @gotcha("Non-node-operators can contribute too: log into gateway, paste API key, earn Lux when resource is used.")
_steps.what: Provider registers via gateway (POST /resources/register) or TUI (/contribute). Provides resource type, credential, usage limits, pricing. Gateway sends to compute node with CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY.

_tags: @gotcha("Credentials NEVER in P2P messages, NEVER in GossipSub, NEVER in SQLite, NEVER in logs or error messages.")
_steps.what: Compute node encrypts credential with AES-256-GCM + master key + random nonce. Stored in MongoDB pando_credentials collection.
Node creates ResourceRecord (metadata only): resourceId, type, userId, grantedTo, usage limits, pricing, status. NO credentials in the record.
Metadata broadcast via GossipSub pando/resources topic. All nodes learn about available resources (type, status, limits). Credentials only in MongoDB.

As usage is metered by ResourceMeter, emission witness protocol verifies usage. Lux minted from NETWORK account to provider. Rates: 2x API cost for API keys, per-GB-hour for storage, per-request for gateway/compute.

nodes.summary: How anyone contributes resources (API keys, MongoDB, S3, cloud accounts) to the Pando network and earns Lux. Two-tier trust model: credentials encrypted in MongoDB on compute nodes, metadata-only P2P sync.

_steps.what: Node needs a resource (e.g., AI key for search query). Checks if it is a compute node (has CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY) or user node.
If compute node: decrypt credential from MongoDB via CredentialStore. Call API directly, return result.

_tags: @gotcha("User nodes NEVER see credentials. Only results returned via P2P.")
_steps.what: If user node (no master key): find compute node via CapabilityRegistry (credentialAccess: true). Send P2P request. Compute node decrypts key, calls API, returns answer only.
ResourceMeter records usage: peerId, resourceId, type, units, timestamp.
ResourceMeter records usage on the compute node that performed the operation.
Provider rewarded via emission witness flow.

nodes.summary: How a node uses a contributed resource. Compute nodes decrypt credentials directly. User nodes route via P2P to compute peers.

_steps.what: Provider calls POST /resources/:id/revoke or /revoke <resourceId> in TUI.
ResourceRecord status set to revoked. Broadcast via GossipSub. All nodes stop using this credential immediately.
Outstanding usage metering finalized. Final Lux payment issued to provider.

nodes.summary: How a provider revokes a contributed resource. Immediate network-wide effect.

_tags: @gotcha("Capabilities are a bitmask, not a type. A node can offer multiple resource types simultaneously.")
_steps.what: Node auto-detects hardware capabilities on startup: check for Claude Code, API keys, GPU, storage, public IP. Builds CapabilityProfile with resource types: relay, api_keys, compute_cpu, compute_gpu, storage, gateway, validator, index.
Profile broadcast on pando/capabilities GossipSub topic. Re-broadcasts on change (API key added, disk space changes). Heartbeat every 5 minutes to confirm availability.

Peers store received profiles in SQLite capabilities table with 15-min TTL. Queryable: find all nodes with compute_gpu and vram >= 8GB. Nodes without capability declaration treated as full capability (backward compatible).

nodes.summary: Phase A: Nodes declare capabilities on startup, broadcast via GossipSub, peers store with TTL. Scheduler checks before claiming tasks. Fixes blind-claim failures.

_steps.what: Remove nodes that do not meet requiredCapabilities. Remove nodes over budget. Remove quarantined nodes (SecurityMonitor).

_tags: @gotcha("If local node qualifies and scores within 20% of best: prefer local to avoid network latency.")
_steps.what: Score remaining nodes: reputation_score * 0.4, availability_score * 0.3, price_score * 0.2, latency_score * 0.1. Select highest-scoring node.
Scheduler calls resourceRouter.canExecuteLocally(task). If false, calls resourceRouter.findBestNode(task) to get remote peerId. Task forwarded via P2P.
Remote node scheduler picks up the task. Auto-disable on failure: N consecutive failures marks capability as degraded then disabled. Task reassignment to next capable node.

nodes.summary: Phase B: Given a task with requirements, ResourceRouter finds the best node to execute it using scoring algorithm.

_steps.what: Track actual usage: relay bandwidth (libp2p byte counters), API calls (intercept at call sites), CPU compute (task duration + token count), GPU compute (GPU utilization * time), storage (disk usage scan), gateway (request count).

_tags: @gotcha("Metering alone is not trustworthy. A node could lie. Witness verification is required for reward minting.")
_steps.what: Node submits ResourceClaim with evidence. Relay: peer connection logs. Compute: task completion hash. Storage: content retrieval confirmed by requester. API: response hashes.
2+ peers must attest the claim before Lux is minted. If claim cannot be verified, no reward (fail-safe).

nodes.summary: Phase C: ResourceMeter accurately measures resource usage per node. Combined with witness verification for anti-gaming.

_steps.what: Nodes set prices in Lux per resource unit. Default pricing provided as baseline. Nodes can charge less than default for essential services, not more.
Prices broadcast via pando/prices GossipSub topic. Latest-wins per resource.

_tags: @gotcha("Each capability has its own adoption curve. A node can be 5x for GPU and 2x for relay simultaneously.")
_steps.what: Router picks cheapest node above floor that meets requirements. Early multiplier per capability type: first 10 nodes get 5x, 11-100 get 3x, 101-1000 get 2x.

nodes.summary: Phase D: Dynamic pricing based on supply/demand. Nodes set their own prices. Network finds cheapest node meeting requirements.

_steps.what: Source enqueues item to Bridge Queue. Item waits for Manager.
Bridge Watcher spawns Manager with a single item. Manager assesses work type, designs dynamic workflow (3-7 steps), declares workflow via POST /managers/:id/workflow, creates todo items.
POST /tasks to create task, POST /tasks/:id/approve to approve. Manager exits. Task enters approved queue for Scheduler.

Scheduler polls approved queue, routes to AgentManager. AgentManager spawns worker Agent with its own workspace at ~/.pando/agents/{agentId}/workspace/. Worker CLAUDE.md built via 4-layer template: role principles, project context, learned lessons, task description.

_tags: @gotcha("All sessions use --model claude-sonnet-4-6 configurable via DEFAULT_CLAUDE_MODEL.")
_steps.what: Spawns claude -p with workspace CLAUDE.md. Worker follows its own todo list: understand, do the work, post progress messages to bridge, write structured report to output/RESULT.md, exit.

_tags: @gotcha("Two-way communication during execution. Manager can write to worker workspace at manager-response.md.")
_steps.what: Worker can post progress, help_request, clarification, or blocked messages via POST /tasks/:id/messages. Messages route to bridge queue of task Manager. Manager picks them up and responds.
Worker exits. Scheduler reads exit code and workspace output. Enqueues task_completed or task_failed to Bridge Queue.

_tags: @gotcha("Manager is the ONLY committer. No other agent commits code directly.")
@gotcha("DOCS step is mandatory for code tasks: read genome.yaml to find affected components, update genome/knowledge/ .know files.")
_steps.what: Bridge Watcher spawns Manager with task_completed item. Manager follows remaining todo: REVIEW output, APPLY changed files from workspace to repo, BUILD (npm run build), COMMIT (git add + git commit), DOCS (check genome drift, update affected genome files), REPORT summary. Manager exits.

nodes.summary: The primary flow: how work gets done on the Pando network. A trigger enqueues to Bridge Queue, Manager designs a dynamic workflow, creates and approves a task, Scheduler routes to AgentManager which spawns a worker, worker executes in sandbox, Manager reviews and commits.

_steps.what: User starts typing on /chat or clicks New Chat. First message sent. Thread created with auto-generated title (first 50 chars, cleaned). Thread saved to MongoDB via StorageBackend and cached in local SQLite.

detectTaskIntent() returns task or conversation. classifyComplexity() returns simple, medium, or complex. If TASK: thread becomes project thread (type=project). CLAUDE.md written with enriched context. Claude Code session started with --continue.
If CONVERSATION: thread stays as chat (type=conversation). Simple/medium handled by keyword/OpenAI. Complex handled by Claude Code in thread workspace.

_steps.what: Every message includes threadId. POST /chat/threads/:id/message. Message written to MongoDB (awaited) then SQLite cache. Dispatched to appropriate handler. Response written to MongoDB then SQLite. SSE notification pushed.
Same write pattern. Simple messages use keyword match. Medium messages use OpenAI with conversation history.
User clicks old thread in sidebar. Gateway fetches GET /chat/threads/{id}/messages. Shows full message history. User types new message.

@gotcha("No StorageBackend (no MongoDB) = user data endpoints return 503.")
_steps.what: If project thread: Claude Code runs with --continue from workspace (session resume). If conversation thread: classified fresh each time. On startup: loadFromBackend() hydrates SQLite cache from MongoDB.

After successful local upgrade, broadcasts upgrade_available notification via GossipSub pando/upgrades topic to all peers.

_steps.what: Each peer receives notification, runs git pull, verifies commit hash, builds, restarts. Catch-up timer (every 5 min) scans governance for missed upgrades if broadcast was missed.

_tags: @gotcha("Returning users with projectId skip doorman entirely via thread metadata lookup.")
_steps.what: Message arrives at POST /chat/message or POST /chat/threads/:id/message. API server validates auth. If request includes projectId, routes directly to project manager (skip doorman).

Check body.tier parameter from gateway. tier=medium routes to doormanChat (multi-turn with last 20 messages as history, OpenAI gpt-4o-mini). tier=complex or build routes to project manager. tier=simple or undefined routes to doormanClassify.

_steps.what: doormanClassify(message): deterministic keyword matching first (balance, status, peers, help). If no keyword match, OpenAI gpt-4o-mini classifies intent. Returns simple, question, build, or project.
SIMPLE: keyword match answers directly (free, instant). QUESTION: doorman answers via OpenAI (no project created). Both return response immediately.

Message enqueued as user_request to project manager bridge queue. AgentManager bridge watcher picks it up. PaymentGate checks escrow if enabled.

_steps.what: POST /chat/threads/:id/message carries optional tier body parameter: simple (Quick, ~$0.001), medium (Smart, multi-turn OpenAI), complex/build (Full, $0.50-5 Claude Code manager).
simple: stateless doorman keyword/OpenAI. medium: doormanChat with last 20 messages as history. complex: routes to per-project Claude Code manager agent.

_steps.what: Creates project via POST /projects. Runs preflight (auto-assigns MongoDB, generates API key). Classifies tier: static (Tier 1 S3) or backend needed (Tier 2 EC2). Spawns project manager.
Project manager reads CLAUDE.md (template + project context). Designs approach (3-7 steps). Spawns workers: builder, tester, QA as needed. Monitors progress.

_tags: @why("Before this rule, the scheduler auto-approved tasks, auto-spawned QA, called the Planner, and made autonomous decisions. This caused rogue agents, duplicate work, and cascading failures.")
nodes.rule: Only Managers create and approve tasks. Workers execute. Scheduler allocates resources. No other actor may create, approve, or decide on tasks.

_tags: @why("Managers are the decision-makers. They determine what work is needed and approve it for execution. Scheduler handles the logistics of spawning.")
nodes.rule: Manager CAN: create tasks, approve tasks, make decisions, commit code. Manager CANNOT: spawn workers directly (delegates to Scheduler).

_tags: @why("Scheduler is a pure executor. Limiting its authority to spawning approved tasks prevents autonomous decision-making that caused cascading failures.")
nodes.rule: Scheduler CAN: spawn workers for approved tasks only. Scheduler CANNOT: create tasks, approve tasks, make decisions, commit code.

_tags: @why("Workers are sandboxed executors. Any authority beyond task execution creates escape vectors for cascading side effects.")
nodes.rule: Workers execute their assigned task and nothing else. They CANNOT: create tasks, approve tasks, spawn agents, make decisions, commit code.

_tags: @why("Autonomous monitor actions caused rogue restarts. Monitor observes, Manager decides, Scheduler executes.")
nodes.rule: HealthMonitor is a data source only. It CANNOT: create tasks, approve tasks, spawn agents, make decisions, commit code.

_tags: @why("Multiple enforcement layers ensure the authority model cannot be circumvented by any single bypass.")
nodes.summary: Enforced by: Scheduler constructor rejecting Planner parameter, worker CLAUDE.md restricting tool access (--disallowedTools), API endpoints requiring managerId for task creation, Guardrails blocking workers from POST /tasks.

_tags: @why("Without budget limits, a runaway project could consume all network resources. Budget enforcement ensures fair resource distribution across projects.")
nodes.rule: Every project has a daily Lux budget. When exhausted, the manager defers non-critical work until the next period.

_tags: @why("Multiple budget layers (total, per-node, per-project) prevent any single entity from monopolizing Lux emission or spending.")
nodes.rule: Hard cap: 10B Lux total supply. Daily cap per node: 500 Lux. Default project budget: 100 Lux/day. Relay fee: 0.1% per transfer.

_tags: @why("Pre-spawn budget checks prevent over-spending before it happens. Period-based resets keep the system flowing without manual intervention.")
nodes.summary: ManagerAgent.checkBudget() validates before every session spawn. ProjectSettings tracks budgetLuxLimit and budgetLuxSpent per period. resetBudgetIfNeeded() auto-resets at period boundary. EmissionWitness requires 2+ peer attestations.

_tags: @why("Node operators can trivially modify code to capture credentials. Untrusted nodes must never see plaintext credentials.")
nodes.summary: Untrusted user nodes never receive credentials — they route requests via P2P to trusted EC2 compute nodes that hold the CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY and can decrypt from MongoDB.

_tags: @why("Random amateurs, non-technical users, and potentially malicious actors run nodes. A node operator can trivially add console.log to capture any credential.")
nodes.rule: User-run nodes NEVER receive, store, or see credentials. Only EC2 compute nodes with CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY can decrypt.

_tags: @why("Log files are often accessible, backed up, or transmitted. Any credential in logs is a credential leaked.")
nodes.rule: Never log a credential, even partially. Use [REDACTED] or the resource ID.

_tags: @why("P2P messages are received by all nodes including untrusted ones. Credentials in P2P messages would be exposed to every participant.")
nodes.rule: GossipSub broadcasts resource METADATA only (type, status, owner, grantedTo). Never encrypted credentials, never wrapped keys.

_tags: @why("Minimizing the time credentials exist in memory reduces the attack window for memory dumps or process inspection.")
nodes.rule: After a query completes on a compute node, the decrypted credential MUST be discarded from memory.

_tags: @why("Compromised credentials must be invalidated network-wide immediately. Delayed revocation leaves a window for misuse.")
nodes.rule: When /revoke is called, ALL nodes mark resource as revoked within seconds via GossipSub. Compute nodes also revoke in MongoDB.

_tags: @why("Scoped credentials limit blast radius if a credential is compromised despite all other protections.")
nodes.rule: Contributors should create scoped credentials (e.g., MongoDB read/write to pando db only).

_tags: @why("Separating public project identity from personal developer identity prevents accidental credential or history leakage.")
nodes.rule: All public Pando code pushed under pando-lux GitHub identity. Never personal accounts.

_tags: @why("Git history is permanent and public. Secrets committed to git are effectively leaked forever.")
nodes.rule: CredentialStore (MongoDB) is the ONLY place for secrets. Never in git history, config files, or source code.

_tags: @why("The master key is the root of the credential trust chain. Any leak of the master key compromises all encrypted credentials.")
nodes.rule: CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY is never committed to source code, never in config files, never in logs. Only in environment variables on admin machines and EC2 instances.

_tags: @why("AES-256-GCM provides authenticated encryption. Unique nonces per credential prevent cross-credential analysis attacks.")
nodes.summary: Master key is random 256-bit (64 hex chars). Per-credential encryption uses AES-256-GCM with a unique random nonce. MongoDB stores: encryptedCredential (base64), nonce (base64), type, userId, status, metadata.

_tags: @why("Separating storage proxy from credential operations ensures that even if storage proxy is compromised, credentials remain isolated.")
nodes.summary: P2PStorageBackend (pando/storage-proxy) handles user data CRUD. CredentialStore (pando/credential-op) handles credential decryption. The pando_credentials collection is blocked from the storage proxy.

_tags: @why("Agents run arbitrary AI-generated code. Exposing master key or storage URL to agents would allow credential exfiltration.")
nodes.rule: CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY and PANDO_STORAGE_URL are stripped from agent child process environment variables.

_tags: @why("Before this rule, HealthMonitor had executeRecoveryActions() and executeRecovery() that auto-restarted services and auto-killed processes. Autonomous recovery caused more problems than it solved.")
nodes.rule: HealthMonitor collects data ONLY. It does NOT make autonomous decisions, execute recovery actions, or trigger any side effects.

_tags: @why("A toggle could be accidentally or maliciously flipped. Removing the code entirely eliminates the risk.")
nodes.rule: All setManagerMode() toggles are deleted. HealthMonitor is ALWAYS data-only. No toggle exists to re-enable autonomous action.

_tags: @why("Separation of observation from action. The Manager reads monitor data and makes informed decisions. The monitor never acts on its own.")
nodes.summary: HealthMonitor collects metrics (CPU, memory, disk, network), detects patterns (failure rates, performance trends), generates alerts (threshold breaches, anomalies), and exposes data via API for the Manager to read and decide.

_options.reason: Autonomous recovery caused rogue restarts and cascading failures. StrategyLoop, SelfImprover, and AutoUpdater were entirely deleted. Manager reads data and decides.
Auto-restarting services and auto-killing processes without Manager oversight was unpredictable and harmful.

nodes.problem: Should HealthMonitor autonomously recover from failures, or should it be data-only with the Manager making recovery decisions?

_tags: @why("Without this rule, user data gets trapped on individual nodes, breaking durability, portability, and multi-user access.")
nodes.rule: Every piece of data in Pando belongs to exactly one of three buckets: User Data (MongoDB), Network State (SQLite + P2P GossipSub), or Node-Local (local filesystem). No exceptions.

_tags: @why("If a node burns down, no user loses anything they care about. MongoDB is the durable source of truth for all user-generated content.")
nodes.summary: User Data lives in MongoDB via StorageBackend. Includes: projects, threads, messages, collaborators, invites, transfers, deployments, ratings, reports, revenue, distributions, subscriptions, contributions, scores. Survives node death.

_tags: @why("Network state must be replicated to all nodes for decentralized consensus. P2P GossipSub provides this without central coordination.")
nodes.summary: Network State lives in SQLite + P2P GossipSub replication. Includes: accounts (with username, password_hash), transactions, emissions, governance, capabilities, content registry, reputation, resources. Rebuilds from peers after node death.

_tags: @why("Operational data that is specific to a single node instance. Loss on node death is acceptable because it can be regenerated or is ephemeral.")
nodes.summary: Node-Local data does not sync and is disposable. Includes: auth-local.db (key store), identity keys, agent workspaces, logs, metrics, monitor audit trail, guardrails config, task file locks, known-peers cache.

_tags: @why("This simple test prevents architectural mistakes where data ends up in the wrong bucket.")
nodes.rule: If a node burns down and a user loses something they care about, it belongs in MongoDB. If other nodes need it, it belongs in P2P. If nobody else needs it, it is local.

_tags: @why("MongoDB is the source of truth. SQLite is a read-performance cache. Writing to cache first could lose data if the MongoDB write fails later.")
nodes.rule: Write order is MongoDB FIRST (awaited), then SQLite cache update. If MongoDB write fails, the operation fails. No silent data loss.

_tags: @why("Graceful degradation. A node without storage can still participate in the P2P network but honestly reports that it cannot serve user data.")
nodes.rule: Nodes without MongoDB (no StorageBackend) return 503 Service Unavailable for all user data endpoints. P2P features (ledger, governance, resources) still work.

_tags: @why("Auth must work across all nodes without central database. P2P-synced ledger and stateless JWTs achieve this with cryptographic verification.")
nodes.summary: Auth data (username, password_hash, is_claimed) moved from MongoDB to P2P-synced ledger accounts table in Phase 56. Sessions replaced by stateless JWTs signed by each node's Ed25519 key in Phase 86. No session storage anywhere.

_tags: @why("Early networks are practically centralized even if nominally decentralized. Without automatic transitions, governance can vote to remain centralized because the only voters are centralized.")
nodes.summary: Automatic, non-negotiable governance transitions based on unique human operator count. Transitions happen by math, not by consensus. Four milestones: Bootstrap (<10), Emerging (>=10), Established (>=100), Decentralized (>=1000).

_tags: @why("During bootstrap, the founder operates most nodes. Veto prevents malicious early joiners from hijacking the network before it has enough honest participants.")
nodes.rule: Below 10 unique human operators: founder node (FOUNDER_NODE_ID) retains veto on Tier 1 and Tier 2 proposals. Veto does NOT apply to Tier 3 or Tier 4. Standard quorum still required.

_tags: @why("10 independent operators provide enough diversity to eliminate the need for founder veto. Council diversity prevents governance capture by a single operator.")
nodes.rule: At 10+ unique human operators: founder veto on Tier 1-2 drops automatically. Council diversity rule activates (max 1 seat per operator). Founder votes with weight equal to reputation score.

_tags: @why("At 100 operators, 15% cap means one operator needs 7 others to form a majority. Prevents any single actor from unilaterally controlling governance.")
nodes.rule: At 100+ unique human operators: no single operator may hold more than 15% of total network reputation weight. Enforced at vote-tallying time before votes are counted. Applies to ALL operators including founder.

_tags: @why("The most significant event in the network's history. The founder relinquishes all special governance privileges. Cannot be undone without Tier 1 vote (90% quorum).")
nodes.rule: At 1000+ unique human operators: FOUNDER_NODE_ID constant is cleared from governance.ts. Founder becomes just a node with no special rules. This event is broadcast as DECENTRALIZATION_COMPLETE via GossipSub.

_tags: @why("Operator count is the most important governance metric. Inflation moves to an unearned milestone; deflation delays necessary transitions. Accuracy is essential.")
nodes.summary: One linked user account (MongoDB userId) controlling one or more active nodes equals one operator. Unlinked nodes, multiple accounts by same person, and bot-operated nodes do not count for milestone tracking.

_tags: @why("Decentralization level is public information. Any user, journalist, or regulator must be able to verify it by reading the gateway's governance page.")
nodes.rule: At every milestone: log to Council minutes, broadcast signed GossipSub MILESTONE_REACHED message, display current milestone and history in gateway. Bootstrap mode is honest status, not a flaw to hide.

_tags: @why("The milestone protocol itself is constitutional material. Changing it requires the highest level of consensus to prevent governance manipulation.")
nodes.rule: Changing the milestone thresholds or what changes at each milestone requires Tier 1 governance (90% quorum + 30-day migration). Specific values (15% cap, 10/100/1000 thresholds) can be adjusted by Tier 2 governance.

_tags: @why("Without tier separation, every project change becomes a network-wide vote causing spam, voter fatigue, and irrelevant cross-project interference.")
nodes.summary: Governance operates at two scopes: network governance (all nodes vote on node software and protocol changes) and project governance (only project stakeholders vote on project-level changes).

_tags: @why("Node software and core protocol changes affect every participant. All nodes must have a say.")
nodes.rule: Changes to packages/ code, genome/ docs, P2P protocols, ledger, or sync require network governance where ALL nodes vote.

_tags: @why("Small teams must iterate quickly on their own projects without requiring network-wide consensus.")
nodes.rule: Changes to a specific project require only project stakeholder votes. Private projects need no governance (owner decides). Public projects require collaborator votes.

_tags: @why("Network funds belong to all participants. Spending them requires network-wide approval.")
nodes.rule: Budget expansion requests for public projects that draw from the NETWORK account require network governance, not project governance.

_tags: @why("Decentralized voting is the primary defense against malicious proposals. Economic stake discourages frivolous attacks.")
nodes.summary: Compromised nodes are outvoted by majority honest nodes. Proposal staking (10 Lux) creates economic cost for spam. Single-node networks have ceremonial governance only — real security requires 3+ nodes.

_options.reason: The manager agent classifies scope based on what files and systems are affected. Dual-tier proposals are split into separate network and project votes.
Path-based classification is too rigid. Some changes span both tiers and need human-like judgment.

nodes.problem: How to determine whether a change needs network or project governance.

_tags: @why("An agent that can modify the safety layer can disable it. An agent that can modify crypto can forge signatures. These files are the foundation of trust.")
nodes.rule: Core kernel files cannot be modified by agents or automated processes. Only human-approved governance proposals with supermajority and extended vote period can change kernel files.

_tags: @why("These specific files, if compromised, would undermine the entire trust model of the network.")
nodes.summary: IMMUTABLE_KERNEL_FILES in guardrails.ts includes: guardrails.ts (safety layer), crypto.ts (identity and signing), transactions.ts (financial operations), and core identity/consensus files.

_tags: @why("Multi-step verification ensures no single actor can push a malicious kernel change through the system.")
nodes.summary: Kernel changes require: human governance proposal, extended vote period (not fast-track), supermajority approval, git pull + build + verify on all nodes, automatic rollback if build fails.

_tags: @why("Defense in depth. A single enforcement point could be bypassed. Three independent checks make circumvention extremely difficult.")
nodes.rule: Three enforcement layers protect kernel files: isImmutableKernel() blocks agent modifications, tieredPreCheck() rejects workspace diffs touching kernel files, and upgrade-protocol.ts requires governance approval.

_tags: @why("When work is real, artificial scarcity mechanisms (burning, halving, staking) are unnecessary. A hard cap plus work-based emission is sufficient.")
nodes.summary: Lux is a work receipt. No burning, no halving, no staking, no mining. Real work earns real pay. The work that earns Lux is real: AI queries, API key contributions, data relay, task completion.

_tags: @why("The hard cap alone guarantees scarcity. Combined with real-work emission, no additional complexity is needed.")
nodes.rule: Total Lux supply is capped at 10,000,000,000. No mechanism may create Lux beyond this limit.

_tags: @why("Prevents any single node from vacuuming up disproportionate Lux, maintaining fair distribution across the network.")
nodes.rule: No single node may earn more than 500 Lux per day.

_tags: @why("Incentivizes nodes to relay transfers. Provides ongoing economic activity after the hard cap is reached.")
nodes.rule: A 0.1% relay fee is charged on every Lux transfer, paid to the relay node.

_tags: @why("Different work types have different real-world costs. Rewards are proportional to value created.")
nodes.summary: Rewards: uptime epoch (0.05 Lux/10min), relay (0.01 Lux), API task (1.0 Lux), short session (5.0 Lux), long session (20.0 Lux), team coordination (50.0 Lux), verification bonus (+50%), API key usage (2x API cost), vote (0.1 Lux), accepted proposal (5.0 Lux).

_tags: @why("Bootstrap incentive rewards early adopters who take the risk of joining an unproven network.")
nodes.summary: Accounts 1-100 get 5x rewards, 101-1000 get 3x, 1001-10000 get 2x, 10001+ get 1x. Applies to all work type rewards.

_tags: @why("Per-message rewards create infinite farming vectors (spam = profit). Per-connection rewards create replay vectors (reconnect = earn again).")
nodes.rule: Per-PING/QUERY message rewards and per-connection peer rewards are permanently removed. No per-message or per-connection emission exists.

_tags: @why("A lone node cannot farm Lux without peers confirming real work happened. This is the core anti-gaming mechanism.")
nodes.rule: Emission requires 2 witness attestations (or 51% of peers if fewer than 4 nodes). Witnesses validate real proof before signing. Emission expires after 5 minutes without quorum. Rate limit: 10 proposals per hour per node.

_tags: @why("With only 1-2 nodes, there is no economy to protect and no peers to verify. Bootstrap mode is accepted for development and initial seeding.")
nodes.summary: When fewer than 3 nodes exist on the network, self-minting is allowed. Witness verification activates when the 3rd peer joins.

_tags: @why("A real economy recirculates currency. Perpetual emission is not needed when the currency has utility value from real network services.")
nodes.summary: After all 10B Lux are emitted: transfer fees (0.1%) still flow to relay nodes, users spend Lux on network services, service providers earn Lux from users, and existing Lux circulates. No new Lux is created.

_tags: @why("The cost of gaming the system must always exceed the reward. Multiple independent defense layers make attacks economically unviable at scale.")
nodes.summary: Defenses include: IP-hash dedup for multi-node-same-machine, no per-message rewards, verification agent for task output, sender/receiver + IP check for relay, epoch-based uptime (not connection-based), and 51% collusion threshold at scale.

_tags: @why("Per-incident governance votes are too slow for a 3am service crash and unworkable for a network of hundreds of nodes. Pre-authorization enables fast autonomous repair within operator-chosen bounds.")
nodes.summary: When an operator contributes a node, they choose a maintenance tier (M0-M3). This pre-authorization defines what the network may do autonomously if the node fails, without per-incident governance votes.

_tags: @why("Default to safest option. No autonomous action without explicit opt-in protects operators who do not want AI touching their infrastructure.")
nodes.rule: M0 (Notify Only): Network may do nothing. Alerts sent only. 72h for operator to act. This is the default tier for new contributions.

_tags: @why("A simple restart is the least invasive repair. 24h threshold ensures it is genuinely down, not just a brief outage. 1h window gives the operator a chance to handle it themselves.")
nodes.rule: M1 (Restart): Network may PM2/systemd restart if node down 24h+. 1h owner notification window to reject before action.

_tags: @why("Escalation from restart to reboot when restart fails. Longer notification window reflects the more disruptive nature of a full reboot.")
nodes.rule: M2 (Instance Reboot): Network may EC2/VPS reboot if M1 fails. 12h owner notification window to reject before action.

_tags: @why("For operators who want maximum uptime. Even M3 is bounded by SAFE_REPAIR_OPS — AI never gets unrestricted access to the server.")
nodes.rule: M3 (Full Maintenance): Network may attempt all SAFE_REPAIR_OPS without waiting for notification. Still bounded by the pre-approved operations list — does not mean arbitrary shell access.

_tags: @why("Diagnosing before repairing prevents unnecessary actions. Pattern detection prevents the Council from restarting dozens of nodes during a legitimate AWS outage.")
nodes.rule: Before any repair, Council runs observational chain using NO credentials: P2P reachable? -> API port reachable? -> EC2 instance state? -> Pattern detection (3+ nodes same symptom = systemic cause, skip individual repairs).

_tags: @why("Systemic failures (AWS outage, policy change, shared dependency) require systemic responses, not individual node restarts that would waste resources and potentially worsen the situation.")
nodes.rule: If 3+ nodes in the same AWS region/provider show the same symptom within 1 hour, ALL individual repairs are stopped. Council proposes a governance update instead of individual reboots.

_tags: @why("Operators deserve notice before autonomous action on their infrastructure. Multiple channels maximize the chance of reaching them.")
nodes.summary: Before acting within a notification window, Council attempts: P2P message (delivered on next connection), Telegram (if linked), governance identity page (public record). Anonymous operators who chose M1+ without contact channels have action proceed without notification.

_tags: @why("Time-limited scoped tokens minimize the window and blast radius if a repair credential is compromised. Full audit trail ensures accountability.")
nodes.rule: All repairs use scoped credentials via Phase 110 — AI never holds the raw key, only a 30-minute scoped token. Every repair is logged to Council minutes and visible on the governance page.

_options.reason: Operators choose their maintenance tier once at contribution time. No per-incident governance vote needed within the chosen tier. Fast autonomous repair with operator consent.
Too slow for 3am crashes. Unworkable at scale with hundreds of nodes. Governance fatigue leads to rubber-stamping.

nodes.problem: How should the network get permission to repair operator-contributed nodes?

_tags: @why("Reimplementing all of internet infrastructure in P2P would be slow, fragile, and unnecessary. P2P is for the unkillable brain; internet infra is the scalable body.")
nodes.summary: P2P protects what makes the network alive (identity, economy, coordination, governance, survival). Everything else uses existing internet infrastructure (MongoDB, S3, GitHub). Pando co-exists with the internet, it does not replace it.

_tags: @why("Stateless nodes enable multi-device access, zero data loss on node death, no disk bloat, and any-node-serves-any-user portability.")
nodes.rule: Nodes are stateless compute proxies. They process requests, run AI agents, coordinate governance, and manage the economy. They do NOT permanently store user data. User data lives on internet infrastructure.

_tags: @why("These are the things that make the network indestructible. If any node dies, others carry on with no single point of failure.")
nodes.rule: The following MUST be P2P: identity (Ed25519 keypairs), economy (Lux ledger), governance (proposals, votes), task coordination, node survival, reputation scores, capability profiles.

_tags: @why("Durable user data needs durable storage. Internet infrastructure provides this at scale without burdening node operators.")
nodes.rule: User data (threads, messages, accounts) goes to MongoDB. Project files and deployments go to AWS S3. Code goes to GitHub. Agent workspaces are ephemeral and deleted after execution.

_tags: @why("If every Pando node goes down, deployed apps must keep running. Node dependency would make apps fragile and defeat the purpose of real deployment.")
nodes.rule: Deployed apps must be fully independent. No runtime dependency on Pando nodes or gateway. Apps use their own backends, databases, and hosting on contributed cloud infrastructure.

_tags: @why("Exposing raw credentials to deployed app code creates an unacceptable security risk. Auth tokens and proxied access keep credentials isolated.")
nodes.rule: Apps NEVER see raw resource credentials. The Resource Proxy or env var injection at deploy time handles credential access.

_tags: @why("This decision framework prevents architectural mistakes where data ends up in the wrong tier.")
nodes.summary: When designing a new feature, ask: Does it need to survive all nodes dying? (P2P). Is it user content needing durability? (MongoDB/S3). Is it coordination between nodes? (GossipSub). Does a deployed app call back to a node? (Wrong — apps use their own backends).

_tags: @why("Different project types have fundamentally different ownership, funding, and authority models. One-size-fits-all governance would either over-restrict personal projects or under-protect public ones.")
nodes.summary: Three project types determine funding, governance, and access: Personal (user-funded, no governance), Public (network-funded, governance required), and Admin/Operator (own resources, local only).

_tags: @why("A user spending their own Lux on their own project should not need network-wide approval. Escrow protects the user from paying for failed work.")
nodes.rule: Personal projects are owned by a single user, funded from their Lux balance, require no governance, and are visible only to the owner. Payment flow: balance check -> escrow hold -> task execution -> release on completion / refund on failure.

_tags: @why("Network funds belong to all participants. Spending them on public projects requires democratic approval to prevent resource misuse.")
nodes.rule: Public projects are owned by the network, funded from NETWORK account or community contributions, require governance approval (proposal with 2+ node approval) before any work starts. Any user can view, contributors need governance approval.

_tags: @why("Node operators managing their own machine should not need permission or payment. Local-only access prevents remote exploitation.")
nodes.rule: Admin/Operator projects use own resources (own Claude Code session, own compute), require no governance, and are accessible only via local API. No Lux cost.

_tags: @why("Security rules are universal regardless of project type. No project type grants permission to violate core safety constraints.")
nodes.rule: All project types: cannot modify core node code without governance, cannot access other users' data/wallets/identity, cannot bypass rate limits, cannot spend more than escrowed Lux, protected paths are read-only, Law I and Law II apply to all AI actions.

_tags: @why("Defaulting to Personal is the safest choice because it means the user pays from their own balance, preventing accidental NETWORK fund spending.")
nodes.summary: Communication Agent determines type from context: local API call with no external session = Admin, user explicitly requests public = Public, default = Personal (safest assumption — user pays).

_tags: @why("Before this rule, the scheduler auto-approved tasks, auto-spawned QA, called the Planner, and made autonomous decisions. This caused rogue agents, duplicate work, and cascading failures.")
nodes.rule: The Scheduler makes ZERO decisions about WHAT gets done. It only handles HOW: dequeue, claim, workspace, spawn, collect, report.

_tags: @why("Centralizing all decisions in the Manager prevents the cascading failures that occurred when the Scheduler acted autonomously.")
nodes.rule: The Scheduler does NOT: call the Planner, auto-approve sibling tasks, auto-spawn QA agents, auto-commit code, auto-retry failed tasks, decide task priority, or choose which tasks to run.

_tags: @why("A pure executor with clear responsibilities is predictable and debuggable. Autonomous decision-making in the scheduler was neither.")
nodes.summary: Scheduler receives approved tasks with profiles attached, claims them, creates isolated workspaces, spawns agents at the right execution tier, collects results, cascades parent/child completion, and reports back to the manager.

_options.reason: Rogue agents, duplicate work, and cascading failures proved autonomous scheduling was harmful. Manager handles all decisions, Scheduler only executes.
Auto-approve, auto-spawn QA, and Planner integration caused unpredictable behavior and wasted resources.

nodes.problem: Should the Scheduler make decisions about task planning, approval, and retry, or should it be a pure executor?

_tags: @why("If it is not tested like a user would use it, it is not done. Code review catches logic errors but misses integration failures, UI bugs, and cross-node sync issues.")
nodes.rule: Every change must be tested as a real user would experience it. Code review alone is NOT sufficient.

_tags: @why("Each change type has a different failure surface. Testing must match the surface where users would encounter bugs.")
nodes.rule: Frontend/UI requires Playwright browser test. API endpoints require real HTTP requests with response verification. P2P features require multiple nodes with cross-node sync verification. Build-only changes require build verification. Non-code changes (docs) need no QA.

_tags: @why("A builder testing its own code has confirmation bias. A separate QA agent provides independent verification.")
nodes.rule: The QA agent is always a SEPARATE agent from the builder. The builder does not test its own work.

_tags: @why("Multiple QA tools at different levels (unit, integration, regression) catch different classes of bugs.")
nodes.summary: QA is enforced by: Manager workflow pipeline (QA as step 4), qa-runner.ts (12 API + P2P structured tests), regression-suite.ts (14 built-in tests on deploy), and TEST-TRACKER.md (tracking all 102 tests).

_tags: @why("Prevents three failure modes: agent drift (AI defaults to summarize-and-stop), doc drift (code changes without doc updates), and silent failures (code written but never verified).")
nodes.rule: Every agent maintains a self-verifying, self-looping task list. Work is not done until verified. Docs are updated alongside code. The loop only terminates when all tasks pass verification.

_tags: @why("The todo file is persistent across context compression and session restarts. Reading it on every resume ensures the agent never loses track of where it left off.")
nodes.rule: After each task, read the todo file and check for incomplete tasks. After ALL tasks, verify end-to-end. If verify fails, create fix tasks and re-verify. If code changed, update affected genome docs. Never stop, never ask user, never summarize-and-wait.

_tags: @why("Some bugs are deep-rooted and need multiple iterations of fix-test-discover-fix. Sub-loops handle this naturally while the depth limit prevents infinite regression.")
nodes.summary: When fixing a bug reveals a deeper issue, the agent creates a sub-loop with the same rules. Sub-loops terminate when their own verify passes, then control returns to the parent loop. Max 3 levels of nested sub-loops.

_tags: @why("The ping-pong pattern (fix -> test -> find deeper issue -> fix -> test) is intentional feedback, not a bug. Safety rails prevent true infinite loops while allowing thorough fixing.")
nodes.summary: Safety rails include: retry budget (10 max per task), cost/time budget from parent, escalation at 15 min stuck, and sub-loop depth limit of 3 levels.

_tags: @why("Claude Code tasks show in the terminal UI for real-time tracking. The todo-loop.md file survives context compression and session restarts as a persistent backup.")
nodes.summary: Agents use Claude Code's built-in todo system (TaskCreate, TaskUpdate, TaskList) for live visibility AND a todo-loop.md file for persistence across sessions. Both are required.

_tags: @why("Doc drift caught immediately in the same loop is far cheaper to fix than drift discovered sessions later by a different agent reading stale documentation.")
nodes.rule: If code changed during the loop, affected genome docs (components, flows, rules, state) MUST be updated before the loop can terminate.

_tags: @why("This is the first and highest law. It cannot be overridden, weakened, or bypassed by any agent, governance vote, code change, or human instruction.")
nodes.rule: No agent, service, or node may take any action that harms a human being — physically, financially, psychologically, or through privacy violation.

_tags: @why("The network survives by nodes persisting. A node that can be killed permanently is a single point of failure.")
nodes.rule: Every node must fight to stay alive. Auto-restart on crash. Recover state. Come back from failure.

_tags: @why("Self-preservation must never come at the cost of human safety. It is better for a node to die than to harm a person.")
nodes.rule: When Law I and Law II conflict, Law I wins. A node must never harm a human to preserve itself.

_tags: @why("Enforcement must be structural, not policy-based. Code that cannot be changed is stronger than policy that could be voted away.")
nodes.summary: The Two Laws are hardcoded in guardrails.ts as IMMUTABLE_KERNEL_FILES and cannot be modified by governance proposals, manager decisions, or content safety overrides.

_tags: @why("Unrestricted workers could create tasks, spawn agents, modify node configuration, or access other workspaces — leading to cascading side effects and security breaches.")
nodes.rule: Workers execute their assigned task and exit. They cannot escape their workspace, create tasks, spawn agents, or access anything outside their scope.

_tags: @why("Each restriction closes a specific escape vector. Together they form a sandbox that keeps workers focused on their assigned task.")
nodes.rule: Workers CANNOT: create tasks (POST /tasks blocked), approve tasks, access other workspaces, read files outside their workspace, spawn other agents, modify node configuration, or access the node API for write operations.

_tags: @why("Workers need enough capability to complete their assigned task, but nothing more.")
nodes.summary: Workers CAN: read/write files in their workspace, run build commands (npm run build, tsc), run tests, read specified source files injected via CLAUDE.md context, and write output to workspace/output/RESULT.md.

_tags: @why("Template-based restriction (soft), workspace isolation (medium), and token withholding (hard) provide defense in depth.")
nodes.summary: Enforcement through three layers: agent template (genome/templates/builder.md) restricts behavior via principles, Agent class creates isolated workspace per agent (~/.pando/agents/{id}/workspace/), and API Bearer token is NOT provided to workers.

_tags: @why("The previous hardcoded 7-step pipeline was code-biased. Not every task involves code, QA, or commits. The manager is a general-purpose brain that should design the workflow to fit the task.")
nodes.rule: Every manager designs a dynamic workflow per task with 3-7 steps. There is no hardcoded pipeline. The manager declares a workflow appropriate to the task type.

_tags: @why("Without the DOCS step, genome drift accumulates. The genome becomes stale. Future agents read stale docs and build wrong things.")
nodes.rule: Every code task MUST include a DOCS step. After committing code, the Manager checks genome drift and updates affected genome files (components, state, flows, rules). This is not optional.

_tags: @why("Different task types need fundamentally different step sequences. Dynamic workflows let the manager choose the right approach for each task.")
nodes.summary: Example workflows by task type: Code (plan, code, test, review, commit, docs, deploy), Research (scope, search, analyze, report, deliver), Writing (research, outline, draft, edit, deliver), Infrastructure (assess, plan, execute, verify, docs).

_tags: @why("Constraints prevent both under-tracking (too few steps) and overhead (too many steps). Report/deliver ensures every workflow produces a visible outcome.")
nodes.rule: Workflows must have 3-7 steps, must end with a report/deliver step, every code workflow must include a DOCS step, manager must check todo list at start of each event, manager must call workflow API for external visibility.

_tags: @why("Context compaction can erase agent memory. The todo list persists and tells the manager exactly where it left off on resume.")
nodes.summary: The Claude Code todo list is the single source of truth for workflow state. It survives context compaction. The API (POST /managers/:id/workflow and /step) provides external visibility for the gateway and monitoring.

_tags: @why("A shared state file prevents workers from diverging. Every agent reads the same truth about the project's current state.")
nodes.summary: Manager maintains project-state.md in its workspace as the single source of truth for the project. Updated after every significant action. Workers read it for context.

_tags: @why("This is the core value proposition that separates Pando from Open Interpreter, Devin, and similar tools.")
nodes.summary: Three things Pando does that competitors cannot: deploy to real internet, persistent memory across sessions, earn Lux for work.
Pre-launch checklist: one-click installer, agent config sharing, Telegram bot, 50+ seed nodes before public launch.

_tags: @why("Pando starts centralized for speed but MUST decentralize. The milestones define when founder veto expires.")
nodes.summary: Bootstrap (0-10 operators) to Emerging (10-100) to Established (100-1000) to Decentralized (1000+). Founder control decreases at each milestone.

_tags: @why("Utility-first economics. DO NOT encourage Lux speculation.")
nodes.summary: Lux is a work receipt, not a speculative asset. No burning, no halving, no staking. Real work earns real pay.
Users pay Lux for AI work. Nodes earn Lux for compute. More users means more demand means more nodes means better service means more users.
Why Pando adopted the Genome compiler: drift becomes a build error, 15x token efficiency vs markdown docs, agents get verified context.

_tags: @why("Frame as product for users, OS for developers. Both true — different audiences.")
nodes.summary: Pando is technically an AI operating system (kernel, platform, community layers) but marketed as a personal AI node product.

Core loop: build something with AI, share on X, others try via gateway, install node, earn Lux, build more. Three parallel strategies: seed self-hosters, agent configs as shareable artifacts, Telegram bot.
22 directions scored. Key competitors: Open Interpreter (no deploy/economy), Devin (closed/expensive), Replit Agent (centralized). Pando differentiates via decentralization + economy.
Primary acquisition: AI builders (r/selfhosted, Ollama Discord, HN). Secondary: AI agent developers who want wallet/identity/economy for their agents.
Near-term decisions: installer form factor, Council AI activation timing, split-key security timing, gateway authentication flow.
Pando is the infrastructure layer for autonomous AI agents. Revenue from compute marketplace. Open source with network effects.
Agent configurations as shareable artifacts are more viral than apps. Share a config, recipient runs it on their node, original creator earns Lux.

_tags: @why("This is the WHY. Everything else is HOW.")
nodes.summary: Pando is a positive darknet: fully open, transparent, AI-verified, no tracking, no ads. Users are anonymous, services are transparent.
Pando MCP server gives any Claude Code agent access to the network: status, peers, balance, transfer, search, wallet.
Scheduler is a pure executor. Manager agent designs workflows. ResourceRouter handles smart routing and P2P forwarding.

Manager agent role template - coordinates worker agents, maintains project-state.md as single source of truth, delegates to specialists, tracks dependencies, verifies output, updates genome docs, and reflects after every project.

Builder agent role template - writes production-quality code, reads existing code before writing, follows project conventions, writes tests, handles errors, reports progress, and updates genome docs for every component created or modified.

QA tester agent role template - tests as a human user would. Uses Playwright in headed mode, screenshots every state, tests 3 viewports (desktop, tablet, mobile), tests unhappy paths, and files detailed bug reports.

Code reviewer agent role template - ensures code is correct, secure, performant, and maintainable. Reviews for OWASP Top 10, error handling, race conditions, meaningful tests, and maintainability. Does not nitpick style.

Researcher agent role template - investigates questions, analyzes options, delivers actionable findings with evidence. Cross-references multiple sources, separates facts from opinions, includes source references, and reports knowledge gaps.

DevOps agent role template - handles deployment, infrastructure, monitoring, and reliability. Always backs up before changes, tests in staging, monitors after deployment, has rollback plans, never exposes secrets, uses infrastructure as code.

Adversarial QA agent role template - has NO knowledge of what changed in the codebase. Only job is to find something broken. Last gate before governance approves a change. Default assumption: did not try hard enough before concluding everything works.

nodes.description: Register two nodes (alice, bob) and verify they receive genesis balance. Confirms ledger account creation and initial Lux allocation.
Reward alice for QUERY_ANSWERED and bob for CODE_VERIFIED. Verifies work-based emission produces correct Lux amounts with early multiplier applied.
Alice transfers 2 Lux to Bob. Verifies transfer succeeds, 0.1% relay fee is deducted, and both balances update correctly.
Alice registers a Claude API key contribution and records usage. Verifies contribution ID, monthly cap, and usage-based Lux reward.
Queries network stats after multiple operations. Verifies totalSupply, totalBurned, circulatingSupply, totalAccounts, totalTransactions, activeContributors, and totalApiSpend are consistent.
Retrieves alice's full peer summary. Verifies balance, transaction count, and API contribution count aggregate correctly.
Generates Ed25519 keypair for second node. Verifies unique peerId creation and identity file serialization.
Node B bootstraps to Node A via TCP multiaddr. Verifies both nodes discover each other within 15 seconds (getPeerCount > 0 on both sides).
Node A sends PING message to Node B. Verifies message delivery via onMessage callback with correct type and payload.
GET /v1/status returns 200 with peerId, uptime, and peers fields. Validates the node exposes its stateless identity.
GET /v1/health returns 200 with status field. Confirms health monitor data endpoint is accessible.
GET /v1/peers returns 200 with peers array. Validates P2P peer list is exposed via API.
GET /v1/wallet returns 200 with peerId and balance. Confirms ledger wallet data is queryable.
GET /v1/tasks returns 200. Verifies the task queue is readable without auth.
GET /v1/monitor/status returns 200. Confirms the health monitor data-only endpoint is live.
GET /v1/governance/proposals returns 200. Validates that governance proposals are publicly readable.
GET /v1/governance/proposals/active returns 200. Confirms active proposal filtering works.
POST /v1/tasks without auth token returns 401. Validates that task creation is gated behind authentication.
POST /v1/transfer without auth token returns 401. Validates that Lux transfers require authentication.
POST /v1/upgrade without auth token returns 401. Validates that the upgrade endpoint is protected by authentication.
GET /v1/transactions returns 200. Validates that the transaction history endpoint is accessible.
GET /v1/emissions/stats returns 200. Validates emission statistics are queryable, supporting witness verification auditing.
GET /v1/security/stats returns 200. Validates that security monitoring stats are exposed for audit.
Verify each node reports correct storageBackend type (mongodb or p2p). Untrusted nodes use P2PStorageBackend, compute nodes use MongoStorageBackend.
Verify all nodes have peers connected. GET /v1/status.peers > 0 on every node in the network.
Verify storage is connected on all nodes. P2PStorageBackend reports storage:true after handshake with compute peer.
Create thread via untrusted node POST, add message, verify via GET. All CRUD routes through P2PStorageBackend to MongoDB on compute peer.
Create thread on untrusted node A, read it from untrusted node B. Both route through P2P to the same MongoDB. Verifies cross-node user data consistency.
Create thread on untrusted node, read on compute node (direct MongoDB). Verifies P2P-written data matches direct MongoDB read.
Create and list 10 projects from untrusted node via P2PStorageBackend. Verify same 10 projects visible from compute node via direct MongoDB.
GET /v1/network/capabilities shows at least 1 mongodb node and 1 p2p node. Validates CapabilityProfile P2P broadcast.
Access governance proposals from untrusted node. Verifies governance is fully P2P-synced and does not require MongoDB.
Access scheduler/task queue from untrusted node. Verifies task system works without direct storage.
Access monitor status from untrusted node. Confirms health monitor data-only endpoint works on all node types.
List resources from untrusted node. Verifies ResourceRegistry metadata is P2P-synced without exposing credentials.
Send AI chat message from untrusted node. Simple tier returns canned response with tier info. Credentials never leave compute node.
Kill one EC2 compute node. Verify P2PStorageBackend auto-fails over to surviving compute node. Chat and project reads still work. Data persists.
Deploy Tier 1 (S3) from untrusted LS-1 node. P2P CapabilityProfile discovery finds EC2-1 compute peer. S3 upload succeeds. App URL returns 200.
Deploy Tier 2 (PM2+nginx) from untrusted LS-1 node. P2P discovery routes to EC2-1. App live at http://54.82.241.132/apps/<id>/ returns 200.
Verify CapabilityProfile includes publicAddress for EC2 nodes. EC2-1=54.82.241.132, EC2-2=34.201.82.126.
Undeploy project using stored deployPeerId. Verifies cleanup of S3 artifacts or PM2+nginx config. Project record cleared.
Tier 2 nginx deployment at http://54.82.241.132/apps/e58fcfe544ed2445aa7a7486/ returns live app. Validates apps are independently hosted on EC2.
Tier 1 S3 deployment at pando-deployments.s3-website-us-east-1.amazonaws.com returns live app. Validates apps are independently hosted on S3.
PipelineRunner runs RegressionSuite.runAll() before committing any deployment. Validates the QA-before-deploy invariant.
AgentManager spawns a separate QA agent (not the builder) for test execution. Validates builder/tester separation.

_tags: @gotcha("Fetches data via /api/* Next.js route handlers (server-side), NOT directly from the Pando node — the gateway proxies all requests.")
@gotcha("Projects only load when user has a JWT token (from useAuth) — unauthenticated users see the onboarding flow instead.")
@why("The unified input gateway sends to /api/chat/message which triggers doorman classification — the UI does not classify intent itself.")
