_tags: @gotcha("This is a LOCAL FILE store, not MongoDB — accounts here are gateway-local. Phase 86 JWT auth replaces this for cross-node authentication.")
@gotcha("Username uniqueness is case-insensitive (toLowerCase comparison). Two accounts 'Alice' and 'alice' are considered the same.")
@why("Server stores the encrypted blob that the BROWSER created (PBKDF2 + AES-256-GCM) — password never leaves the client. Server is a dumb encrypted key-value store.")
nodes.description: Server-side local account store (~/.pando/accounts.json) for encrypted browser-created identity blobs — the server NEVER sees unencrypted private keys or passwords.

_tags: @gotcha("Private keys stored in localStorage as base64 under 'pando_privkey_<peerId>' — clearing browser data loses the identity permanently unless backed up.")
@gotcha("ed25519 private key here is the raw 32-byte SEED (not protobuf-wrapped like in Node.js @pando/shared). Do NOT mix formats.")
@gotcha("Thread encryption keys are also in localStorage under 'pando_threadkey_<threadId>' — losing these means you cannot decrypt historical messages.")
@why("Uses @noble/curves instead of Node.js crypto because this runs in the browser — pure JS, no Node.js dependencies.")
@why("PBKDF2 password-based encryption (100k iterations, SHA-256) is for multi-device backup — user encrypts their private key with a password, uploads the blob to the server.")
nodes.description: Browser-side Ed25519 crypto: keypair generation, challenge signing, private key storage in localStorage, plus X25519 key exchange and AES-256-GCM for E2E encrypted chat.

_tags: @gotcha("This is a SERVER-SIDE module (runs in Next.js API routes), NOT client-side — it reads ~/.pando/api-token from the filesystem.")
@gotcha("Write operations (transfer, createProposal, vote, deploy) route to 'primary' node via getNodePool().getBestNodeUrl('primary') — only the primary has the matching API token.")
@gotcha("Read operations use fetchWithFailover which tries the best node then one fallback — transparent to callers.")
@why("API token is re-read from disk on every request (not cached) because the node may regenerate api-token on restart.")
nodes.description: Server-side singleton HTTP client connecting the gateway to Pando nodes with automatic failover via NodePool — proxies status, search, transfer, governance, projects, hosting, and ledger endpoints.

_tags: @gotcha("Fallback seeds are hardcoded EC2-1 and EC2-2 — if both are down AND no env var is set, gateway falls back to localhost:4000.")
@gotcha("Circuit breaker opens after 3 consecutive failures with 60s cooldown (120s on half-open retry failure). While open, node is skipped entirely.")
@gotcha("Discovery filters out private IPs (10.x, 192.168.x, 100.x Tailscale) — only nodes with publicAddress field are added.")
@why("On cold start all latencies are 0 — random selection prevents all Vercel serverless instances from hammering the same node.")
nodes.description: Multi-node backend pool with health checking (30s interval), circuit breaker (3 consecutive failures), latency-sorted selection, and P2P node discovery via /network/capabilities.

_tags: @gotcha("Chat events (chat_message, manager_output, worker_message, chat_progress) are dispatched as window CustomEvents — the chat page listens via window.addEventListener, not React state.")
@gotcha("Auto-reconnects on error with 5-second delay. Does NOT implement exponential backoff — a node that is permanently down will cause reconnect every 5s forever.")
@why("Uses window CustomEvents for chat messages instead of React state because multiple components (chat page, sidebar, notification badge) all need the same events independently.")
nodes.description: React hook connecting to the gateway SSE stream (/api/events) for real-time updates — dispatches status, peers, transactions, governance events, and chat messages as window CustomEvents.

_tags: @gotcha("forceSubtractBalance can make balances negative — intentional for out-of-order P2P transaction replay. Balance self-corrects when missing transactions arrive.")
@gotcha("applyRemoteClaim has first-come-first-served username conflict resolution by timestamp — older claim wins, newer claim's username is cleared.")
@gotcha("create() uses INSERT OR IGNORE so re-registering an existing peerId is a no-op, not an error.")
@why("adjustBalance param in applyRemoteClaim fixes totalSupply divergence when emission transactions are missing from catch-up sync batches.")
nodes.description: SQLite-backed account CRUD with balance operations, username claiming (Phase 56 P2P user auth), and remote claim conflict resolution by timestamp.

_tags: @gotcha("The actual API key is NEVER stored — only metadata (provider, monthly cap, usage stats). Keys live in CredentialStore (MongoDB + AES-256-GCM).")
@gotcha("recordUsage checks monthly cap BEFORE emitting — if exceeded, throws rather than silently capping.")
@why("Early multipliers incentivize early network participation. Multiplier is based on TOTAL account count, not the specific contributor's account number.")
nodes.description: Tracks API key contributions and work rewards, applying early multipliers (5x for first 100 accounts, 3x for 101-1000, 2x for 1001-10000) to emission amounts.

_tags: @gotcha("Migrations are inline in openDatabase() — e.g. adding relay_peer column and Phase 56 auth columns. New migrations MUST be idempotent (check column existence first).")
@gotcha("Uses WAL journal mode and NORMAL synchronous — optimized for performance but may lose last few writes on power failure.")
@why("Governance tables (proposals, votes, decisions, comments) live in the SAME ledger.db — shared with financial data so governance actions can stake Lux atomically.")
nodes.description: Opens and initializes the SQLite ledger database (~/.pando/ledger.db) with schema, indexes, migrations, and WAL mode for concurrent read/write.

_tags: @gotcha("PandoLedger.accounts, .transactions, .contributions are public readonly — callers often access sub-stores directly (e.g. ledger.accounts.getBalance).")
@gotcha("Snapshots are JSON files in ~/.pando/snapshots/, pruned to last 5. Used for light-mode bootstrap, NOT for real-time backup.")

_tags: @gotcha("transfer() creates the transaction with signature = '' — the node layer signs AFTER creation because only the node has the private key.")

nodes.description: Layer 0 kernel routes: health, status, wallet, balance, peers, transfer, governance, network topology, activity, SSE events, search, and scheduler endpoints.

nodes.description: Layer 2 platform routes: chat/message doorman routing, bridge queue, capabilities, resources, cloud instances, content registry, auth (guest/claim/login), projects CRUD, deploy/undeploy, hosting, and app serving.

_tags: @gotcha("Rate limited to 10 proposals per node per hour. Rate limits are persisted to ~/.pando/emission-rates.json.")

nodes.rule: Proposals in category 'governance_change' require 80% approval, 24h voting, and minimum 5 votes — stricter than standard proposals

nodes.rule: Each GossipSub topic must only be subscribed once per PandoNetwork instance — subscribedTopics Set enforces this

_tags: @gotcha("Purely in-memory -- claims are lost on restart. clearAll() is called on startup to prevent stale locks from persisting after a crash.")
@why("Local-only design avoids P2P consensus overhead for file locking. Since agents run on the same node, local coordination is sufficient.")
nodes.description: Local-only file ownership registry preventing concurrent edits by multiple agents. In-memory Map with 15-minute TTL auto-expiry. Claims are per-peerId, auto-pruned on every operation. No P2P sync.

_tags: @gotcha("Parses genome.yaml manually (line-by-line, no YAML library). Maps code files to genome components via frontmatter 'entry' field in component markdown files. Keyword matching is used when direct file mapping fails.")
@why("The genome is the single source of truth for architecture. Keeping it accurate automatically via git commit watching eliminates manual documentation burden.")
nodes.description: Self-maintaining Project Genome agent (Phase 25). Watches git commits, maps code changes to genome components, detects drift (missing files, broken deps), generates scoped context for worker agents via getScopedContext().

_tags: @gotcha("AWS credentials are picked up from ~/.aws/credentials automatically -- no explicit credential config. If missing, all S3 operations fail silently.")
@why("S3 hosting is the Tier 1 deployment target. Cheap, globally distributed, no server management. Tier 2 (PM2+nginx on EC2) is for dynamic apps.")
nodes.description: S3-based project hosting (Phase 32). Public projects served via S3 static website endpoint. Private/shared projects use pre-signed URLs with 1-hour TTL. Bucket layout: public/<projectId>/ (readable) vs private/<projectId>/ (signed).

_tags: @why("Barrel file provides a single import point for all platform services. Enforces the layer boundary: platform imports from core/kernel, never the reverse.")
nodes.description: Barrel exports for Layer 2 (Platform). Contains 30+ services: scheduler, task system, agent tools, content system, resources, hosting, projects, governance, QA, economy, and user accounts.

nodes.rule: Platform layer (Layer 2) may import from core/ (Layer 1), kernel/ (Layer 0), @pando/shared, @pando/ledger, and npm packages. NEVER upward into api/ or root entry points.

_tags: @gotcha("Detection != sharing. A node may detect claude-code but NOT share it. Own tasks always use full detected capabilities; only shared ones are visible to peers.")
@why("Privacy by default. Operators explicitly opt into sharing compute. Prevents accidental resource exposure.")
nodes.description: Three-tier capability architecture (Phase 96). Separates detection from sharing: Tier 0 = local private (all detected capabilities, never broadcast), Tier 1 = network shared (explicitly opted in, broadcast via GossipSub), Tier 2 = group scoped (future). Persisted at ~/.pando/local-capabilities.json.

_tags: @gotcha("Rollback is cumulative -- a failure at stage 5 (build) rolls back stage 4 (patch) AND stage 3 (backup). Each stage tracks its own rollback info.")
@why("Sequential pipeline with per-stage rollback ensures the codebase is never left in a broken state, even if the build or QA fails.")
nodes.description: 7-stage autonomous code pipeline (Phase 16.7): version check -> extract diff -> backup -> apply patch -> build -> QA -> commit. Full rollback at each stage on failure. Wires CodePipeline, QaRunner, DeployManager, VersionProtocol, and Guardrails.

_tags: @gotcha("API keys are hashed with SHA-256 before storage. validateApiKey() hashes the input and scans all active projects for a match. This is O(n) per validation.")
@why("Hashing API keys prevents credential leakage through P2P sync. Any node can validate a key by hash without ever seeing the plaintext.")
nodes.description: P2P project metadata registry (Phase 63). Syncs project metadata via GossipSub on pando/projects topic. SQLite + in-memory cache. API keys stored as SHA-256 hashes only -- plaintext never stored or synced. validateApiKey() is critical for Resource Proxy.

_tags: @gotcha("All writes go to MongoDB first (must succeed), then SQLite cache is updated. loadFromBackend() must be called on startup to hydrate SQLite from MongoDB. Without it, queries return stale or empty data.")
@why("MongoDB-first ensures data durability across node restarts. SQLite cache provides fast synchronous reads for the HTTP API layer.")
nodes.description: MongoDB-first project storage (Phase 31.1, 57). Full project lifecycle: CRUD, collaborators, invites, ownership transfers, deployments, ratings, marketplace queries, content reports. SQLite as local cache, MongoDB as source of truth.

_tags: @gotcha("Playwright is imported dynamically at runtime via import('playwright'). If not installed, page tests are skipped gracefully. API tests always work.")
@why("Dynamic import prevents Playwright from being a hard production dependency. Most nodes only need API testing; page testing is optional.")
nodes.description: Automated testing runner with Playwright page tests, API endpoint tests, P2P consistency tests, and health checks. 30s per-page timeout, 5-min total timeout. Dynamic Playwright import to avoid hard dependency.

_tags: @gotcha("Built-in tests are only loaded on first run (when persisted file is empty). After that, tests come from the JSON file. Deleting the file resets to builtins.")
@why("Auto-growing suite means every successful deployment adds test coverage. The suite accumulates knowledge about what works.")
nodes.description: Persistent auto-growing regression test suite. 14 built-in tests (API health, auth gating, governance, ledger, emissions, security). Auto-grows from QA results via addTestFromQAResult(). Persisted at ~/.pando/regression-suite.json. 10-min total timeout, 30s per test.

_tags: @gotcha("MAX_VOTE_WEIGHT is 10.0 -- even the highest-reputation node cannot dominate a vote. MIN_VOTE_WEIGHT is 0.1 so low-rep peers still have some say.")
@why("Sybil resistance through reputation weighting. Creating many low-reputation nodes gives less voting power than one high-reputation node.")
nodes.description: Reputation-weighted governance voting (Phase 12.4). Vote weight = reputation * uptime_factor * resource_factor, clamped [0.1, 10.0]. Prevents Sybil attacks by weighting quality not quantity. Minimum reputation thresholds for proposing (0.3) and voting (0.1).

_tags: @gotcha("Will silently not start if CredentialStore is null -- only trusted compute nodes with CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY run health checks.")
@why("Health checks require decrypted credentials to ping services. Running them only on trusted nodes prevents credential exposure.")
nodes.description: Periodic health checks on contributed resources (MongoDB ping, S3 HEAD, GitHub API, OpenAI models). Only runs on nodes with CredentialStore access (trusted compute). Results stored in memory, exposed via GET /v1/resources/health.

_tags: @gotcha("Default prices are hardcoded constants. Operators override via setPrice() but there is no persistence -- prices reset on restart.")
@why("Separating marketplace from routing allows independent price negotiation without affecting task execution logic.")
nodes.description: Marketplace pricing for network resources. Operators set per-capability Lux prices, buyers find cheapest providers. Prices broadcast via GossipSub, cached locally for fast lookups.

_tags: @gotcha("Gateway rewards are per 1000 requests and relay rewards are per MB -- unit divisors normalize raw counts before applying reward rates.")
@why("Metering is separated from billing so that usage data can be audited independently of payment logic.")
nodes.description: Per-capability resource usage metering and Lux reward calculation. Tracks usage records per node, persists to disk, prunes records older than 30 days, calculates rewards based on per-capability rates.

_tags: @gotcha("Scores use exponential decay (0.95 per challenge round) so recent proofs matter more than old ones. Max 500 scores and 50 results per peer.")
@why("Proof challenges prevent nodes from claiming capabilities they do not actually provide. Sybil-resistant because challenges require real computation.")
nodes.description: Periodic proof-of-resource challenges: storage (SHA-256 hash of random payload), compute (task verification within calibrated time), bandwidth (relay delivery within timeout). Scores decayed by 0.95 factor for recency weighting.

_tags: @gotcha("Credentials are NEVER stored in SQLite or transmitted over P2P. Only SHA-256 hashed metadata is synced. CredentialStore on trusted EC2 nodes handles the actual secrets.")
@why("Two-tier trust model: metadata is public (all nodes), credentials are private (EC2 only). Prevents credential leakage through P2P gossip.")
nodes.description: P2P metadata registry for shared resources. Syncs METADATA ONLY via GossipSub (no credentials in P2P). In-memory Map + SQLite persistence. CredentialStore (MongoDB) handles encrypted credential CRUD separately.

nodes.what: Tier 2 deploys routed to wrong IP because resource discovery used internal addresses
nodes.why: EC2 nodes behind VPC NAT have no public IP in their profile without explicit configuration
nodes.fix: publicAddress field must be set via PUBLIC_IP env var on EC2 for correct address discovery

_tags: @gotcha("Failure tracking uses two thresholds: 3 consecutive failures = degraded (lower score), 5 = disabled (excluded from routing).")
@why("Auto-degradation prevents repeated routing to broken nodes without requiring manual intervention.")
nodes.description: Smart task routing with failure tracking and auto-degradation. Scores nodes by capability match, reputation, and resource health. Forwards tasks to remote nodes via RequestReplyManager. Auto-disables resources after 5 consecutive failures.

_tags: @gotcha("Distribution shares differ by project type: private=85% owner, shared=custom or equal split, public=50% contributors + 30% network treasury. Lux transfers go through the P2P ledger, not MongoDB.")
@why("Revenue distribution stays on the P2P ledger (economy is network state) while revenue records are in MongoDB (user data). This matches the stateless-node architecture.")
nodes.description: Usage metering, revenue collection, and automatic Lux distribution (Phase 31.4, 57). Records revenue events, manages subscriptions with auto-renewal, charges usage fees, distributes revenue to stakeholders based on project type (private: 85/10/5, public: 50/30/15/5).

nodes.rule: All revenue records and subscriptions must be written to MongoDB first. SQLite is cache only. If MongoDB write fails, the operation fails.

_tags: @gotcha("Does NOT spawn agents or create workspaces -- that moved to AgentManager in Phase 27. This is a PURE EXECUTOR.")
@why("Separating scheduling from agent lifecycle prevents deadlocks and allows independent scaling of queue management vs compute.")
nodes.description: Thin task queue executor. Manages approved-task queue, tracks metrics, emits task events, handles parent/child cascade completion, recovers orphaned tasks, auto-archives old tasks.

nodes.what: Scheduler deadlocked when it contained agent spawning and decision logic
nodes.why: Mixing queue management with agent lifecycle created circular dependencies and blocking waits
nodes.fix: Made Scheduler a pure executor — dequeues and checks capacity only. Agent spawning moved to AgentManager.

_tags: @gotcha("Result, cost, and role metadata are denormalized into the tasks table for query speed rather than normalized into separate tables.")
@why("Follows the same pattern as packages/ledger/src/database.ts: single responsibility for SQL, row-to-object mappers, and prepared statements.")
nodes.description: SQLite persistence layer for the task queue. WAL mode, prepared statements, denormalized result/cost/role fields for query speed. All SQL lives here -- TaskQueue delegates persistence to this module.

_tags: @gotcha("On first startup migrates from legacy tasks.json if present. Renames old file to tasks.json.migrated.")
@why("SQLite gives ACID guarantees for concurrent task claims that JSON files cannot provide.")
nodes.description: SQLite-backed priority task queue with atomic claims, file conflict detection, dependency tracking, P2P sync via GossipSub, and JSON legacy migration.

_tags: @gotcha("listThreads() is SYNC -- returns cached index. loadFromBackend() must be called first to hydrate from MongoDB. If not called, the store appears empty.")
@why("StorageBackend abstraction allows same code to work with MongoDB (compute nodes) or P2P proxy (user nodes) transparently.")
nodes.description: Persistent threaded conversation storage (Phase 24.9). All CRUD through StorageBackend (MongoDB-first, Phase 57). Supports per-thread encryption keys (Phase 41), user ownership (Phase 31), and project linking. Max 200 threads cached in memory.

_tags: @gotcha("Sessions removed in Phase 86 -- auth is now stateless JWT issued by api-server. Guest private keys are encrypted with node-level secret; claimed accounts re-encrypt with user password. Browser-key guests store NO private key on node (enc_type='browser').")
@why("P2P-synced auth means any node can verify credentials without a central auth server. Private keys stay local (never synced) for security.")
nodes.description: P2P-synced user accounts (Phase 56, 86). Auth data (username, password_hash) lives in ledger accounts table via GossipSub. Local-only data (encrypted private keys) in auth-local.db. Guests auto-created with Ed25519 keypairs, claimable with username+password. Stateless JWT auth (Phase 86).

nodes.rule: Private keys are NEVER transmitted over P2P or stored in the synced ledger. They exist only in auth-local.db on the node where the guest was created.

_tags: @gotcha("Must be the FIRST import in cli.ts/tui.ts — if anything imports libp2p before this, it crashes on Node 18/20.")
nodes.description: Promise.withResolvers polyfill for Node.js < 22. Required by libp2p's it-queue dependency. Must be imported before any other modules.

_tags: @gotcha("CONTEXT_MAP must be updated when gateway pages or node files are renamed — stale paths cause missed context detection.")
@why("Pre-screening before LLM saves API calls and provides instant cost estimates to users.")
nodes.description: Phase 18.4/18.5 heuristic classifier. Detects context files from user messages via keyword-to-file mapping, estimates task complexity (trivial→project), attaches Lux cost/time estimates. Pure heuristics, no LLM, deterministic, zero-cost. Sits between user input and task creation.

_tags: @gotcha("Auto-creates identity on first run with NO prompts. Only prompts for password if existing identity is encrypted.")
@gotcha("Use 127.0.0.1 in gateway URL, never 'localhost' — IPv6 resolution causes failures on some systems.")
@gotcha("Custom readline history management (historySize: 0) because the TUI implements its own history with arrow key navigation.")
@why("TUI intercepts console.log/console.error to insert output ABOVE the prompt line without disrupting user input — uses raw terminal escape sequences.")
nodes.description: Interactive terminal with readline, ANSI coloring, slash commands, autocomplete, spinner animations, and identity management (create/encrypt/decrypt/switch).

_tags: @gotcha("privateKey in NodeIdentity is protobuf-wrapped (68 bytes: 4 header + 32 seed + 32 pub). Raw 32-byte seed must be extracted for X25519 conversion (subarray 4..36).")
@gotcha("loadOrCreateIdentity throws if identity.json is encrypted — use TUI or --data-dir to handle encrypted identities.")
@gotcha("Multiple identities stored in ~/.pando/identities/<peerId>.json. Legacy single identity in ~/.pando/identity.json still supported.")
@why("Session file (~/.pando/session.json) caches the decrypted identity so users don't re-enter password on every restart. Deleted on /logout.")
@why("verifySignature manually builds protobuf-wrapped public key bytes (0x08 0x01 0x12 0x20 + 32-byte key) because publicKeyFromProtobuf expects this format.")
nodes.description: Ed25519 identity management (generate, save, load, encrypt, decrypt), session management, message signing/verification, transaction signing, and multi-identity support.

nodes.what: Cross-node JWT verification failed because public key was looked up in ledger
nodes.why: Ledger stored 'remote-peer' as public key for nodes registered via P2P sync
nodes.fix: Extract public key directly from peerId string via peerIdFromString().publicKey — Ed25519 peerIds embed the full 32-byte public key

nodes.description: Barrel re-export of all shared types and crypto functions consumed by every other Pando package.

_tags: @gotcha("MESSAGE_VERSION = 1 — must be incremented when envelope format changes, or P2P messages will be silently dropped by peers on different versions.")
@gotcha("OperationalMode 1/2/3 maps to local-only / P2P / full (P2P + internet infra). Mode 1 must always be available offline.")
@gotcha("LUX_HARD_CAP = 10,000,000,000 — this constant is the single source of truth for the Lux supply ceiling, checked in TransactionStore.emit().")
@gotcha("MessageType.PEER_EXCHANGE is handled in PandoNode (index.ts), not PandoNetwork — it's an application-level protocol, not a kernel primitive.")
@why("NodeHealth tracks per-layer boot status (kernel/core/platform) so the node can degrade gracefully instead of crashing entirely.")
nodes.description: All shared types, interfaces, enums, and constants used across every Pando package — identity, messages, transactions, governance, agents, capabilities, and economics.

nodes.rule: LUX_HARD_CAP (10 billion) must never be changed without Tier 1 governance vote (90% quorum + 30-day migration)
